old: They will never be admitted into any house in this neighborhood.
new: There is one house in this neighborhood they will never be admitted into.
source: Into _one_ house in this neighbourhood they shall never have admittance.
reason: Candidate bans them from every house in the neighborhood; the source bars them from one house only (Longbourn), which is the point of Mr. Bennet's dry emphasis and of the next sentence.

old: unimaginable stubbornness
new: unimaginable resentment
source: such a point of inconceivable resentment
reason: Mrs. Bennet reads his refusal as resentment (anger at Lydia), not stubbornness; the candidate changes the motive she attributes to him.

old: the weeks of living with Wickham
new: the two weeks of living with Wickham
source: living with Wickham a fortnight before they took place
reason: The source specifies a fortnight; 'the weeks' drops the number.

old: to ask him to settle Wickham's various debts in and near Brighton, for which I have pledged myself
new: to ask him to assure Wickham's various creditors in and near Brighton of speedy payment, for which I have pledged myself
source: to request that he will satisfy the various creditors of Mr. Wickham in and near Brighton with assurances of speedy payment, for which I have pledged myself
reason: Colonel Forster is asked only to reassure the creditors that Gardiner (i.e. Darcy) will pay; the candidate has Forster settling the debts himself.

old: was not nearly as warm
new: was not quite so warm
source: was not quite so cordial
reason: Austen's understatement ('not quite so cordial') is inflated to 'not nearly as warm', losing the dry irony.

old: by walking away
new: by running away
source: by running away
reason: Source says she ran away; 'walking' changes the comic haste and her agitation.

old: If you genuinely don't understand me, forgive my frankness.
new: If you choose not to understand me, forgive my impertinence.
source: If you do not choose to understand me, forgive my impertinence.
reason: Mrs. Gardiner suggests Elizabeth may be pretending not to understand; 'genuinely don't understand' removes that teasing suspicion.

old: His stated reason was his conviction that Wickham's worthlessness had not been made known widely enough to prevent any young woman of good character from trusting him.
new: His stated reason was his conviction that it was his own fault that Wickham's worthlessness had not been made known widely enough to prevent any young woman of good character from loving or trusting him.
source: The motive professed was his conviction of its being owing to himself that Wickham's worthlessness had not been so well known as to make it impossible for any young woman of character to love or confide in him.
reason: Drops 'owing to himself' (Darcy's self-blame, the core of his professed motive) and 'love'.

old: a problem he had helped to create
new: a wrong he had brought about himself
source: an evil which had been brought on by himself
reason: Darcy takes the whole blame ('brought on by himself', 'imputed the whole'); 'helped to create' dilutes it to partial responsibility.

old: and return to her family, offering
new: and return to her family as soon as they could be persuaded to take her back, offering
source: return to her friends as soon as they could be prevailed on to receive her
reason: Drops the condition that her family would first have to be persuaded to receive her, a real social implication of her disgrace.

old: but I won't tell you how little I was satisfied with her behavior while she stayed with us, except that I saw from Jane's letter last Wednesday that her conduct since returning home has been equally bad, so
new: but I wouldn't tell you how little I was satisfied with her behavior while she stayed with us if I hadn't seen from Jane's letter last Wednesday that her conduct since returning home has been just the same, and therefore
source: but I would not tell you how little I was satisfied with _her_ behaviour while she stayed with us, if I had not perceived, by Jane's letter last Wednesday, that her conduct on coming home was exactly of a piece with it, and therefore what I now tell you can give you no fresh pain.
reason: Candidate garbles the conditional into 'I won't tell you ... except that', which is self-contradictory; the source says she tells it only because Jane's letter shows Elizabeth already knows.

old: I thought him very reserved; he hardly ever mentioned your name. But reserve seems to be the fashion.
new: I thought him very sly; he hardly ever mentioned your name. But slyness seems to be the fashion.
source: I thought him very sly; he hardly ever mentioned your name. But slyness seems the fashion.
reason: 'Sly' is Mrs. Gardiner's tease that Darcy is hiding his feelings for Elizabeth (and that Elizabeth is too); 'reserved' flattens the joke into a neutral character note.

old: —though I could take it in on my way to Newcastle
new: —otherwise I could take it in on my way to Newcastle
source: or else I could take it in my way to Newcastle
reason: 'Or else' = otherwise: he won't go because it would be too much for him; 'though' suggests he still might.

old: And there was not no truth in that.
new: And it wasn't entirely without foundation.
source: and it was not wholly without foundation
reason: The double negative 'not no truth' reads as an error and obstructs; also loses 'wholly'.

old: her neighbors might all see Mr. Bingley before they did
new: her neighbors might all see Mr. Bingley before they did because of it
source: her neighbours might all see Mr. Bingley, in consequence of it, before _they_ did
reason: Drops the causal link: the neighbors will see him first because of Mr. Bennet's refusal to call, which is why it mortifies her.

old: in her mother's house
new: in her mother's presence
source: he could not in her mother's presence be what he was before her uncle and aunt
reason: The constraint is Mrs. Bennet's presence (the contrast is with the uncle and aunt as company), not the house.

old: Her calculating mother had the same idea and refrained
new: Her prudent mother, occupied by the same idea, refrained
source: Her prudent mother, occupied by the same ideas, forbore to invite him to sit by herself.
reason: Austen's ironic 'prudent' is turned into an explicit narrator judgment ('calculating'), making the irony overt and harsher.

old: expect a renewed proposal
new: expect a renewal of his love
source: How could I ever be foolish enough to expect a renewal of his love?
reason: Elizabeth doubts that his love could revive, not merely that he would propose again; the next sentence handles the proposal separately.

old: unless Mr. Darcy returned later than planned
new: unless Mr. Darcy returned before the time he had given
source: unless Mr. Darcy returned within the stated time
reason: Inverted: Elizabeth's joke is that all will be settled unless Darcy comes back within his ten days to interfere again; the candidate has it reversed.

old: She did seriously believe, however,
new: Seriously, however, she felt fairly sure
source: Seriously, however, she felt tolerably persuaded that all this must have taken place with that gentleman's concurrence.
reason: Loses the hedge 'tolerably persuaded' and the 'Seriously' marker that signals the previous sentence was a joke.

old: that there was reason to fear her mother had been too clever for her own good
new: that there was reason to fear her mother had been too clever for her
source: there was reason to fear that her mother had been too ingenious for her
reason: Source: her mother outwitted Elizabeth; 'too clever for her own good' says the scheme backfired on Mrs. Bennet, the opposite of what happened.

old: clearly in the middle of an earnest conversation
new: as if in earnest conversation
source: as if engaged in earnest conversation
reason: Drops the 'as if' hedge; Elizabeth infers the conversation, she does not know it.

old: who like the others had sat down
new: who like Jane had sat down
source: Bingley, who as well as the other had sat down
reason: 'The other' is Jane; only two people are in the room, so 'the others' misstates who sat down.

old: he could have chosen so much more advantageously.
new: he could have chosen so much more advantageously in many ways.
source: since he might have chosen so much more advantageously in many respects
reason: Drops Jane's qualification 'in many respects', making her self-deprecation absolute.
